kings1.17.p1.b1.text: Now Elijah the Tishbite, who was among the settlers of Gilead, said to Ahab,

kings1.17.p1.b2.text: “As surely as the LORD lives—the God of Israel before whom I stand…”

kings1.17.p1.b3.text: “…there will be neither dew nor rain in these years except at my word!”

kings1.17.p2.b1.text: “Leave here, turn eastward, and hide yourself by the Brook of Cherith, east of the Jordan.

kings1.17.p2.b2.text: And you are to drink from the brook, and I have commanded the ravens to feed you there.”

kings1.17.p2.b3.text: The ravens would bring him bread and meat in the morning and evening, and he would drink from the brook.

kings1.17.p3.b1.text: Some time later, however, the brook dried up because there had been no rain in the land.

kings1.17.p3.b2.text: “Get up and go to Zarephath of Sidon, and stay there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to provide for you.”

kings1.17.p4.b1.text: “Please bring me a little water in a cup, so that I may drink.”

kings1.17.p4.b2.text: “Please bring me a piece of bread.”

kings1.17.p4.b3.text: “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have no bread—only a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in a jug…”

kings1.17.p4.b4.text: “…prepare a meal for myself and my son, so that we may eat it and die.”

kings1.17.p5.b1.text: “Do not be afraid… But first make me a small cake of bread from what you have, and bring it out to me. Afterward, make some for yourself and your son…”

kings1.17.p5.b2.text: “…The jar of flour will not be exhausted and the jug of oil will not run dry until the day the LORD sends rain upon the face of the earth.”

kings1.17.p5.b3.text: The jar of flour was not exhausted and the jug of oil did not run dry, according to the word that the LORD had spoken through Elijah.

kings1.17.p6.b1.text: Later, the son of the woman who owned the house became ill, and his sickness grew worse and worse, until no breath remained in him.

kings1.17.p6.b2.text: “O man of God… what have you done to me? Have you come to remind me of my iniquity and cause the death of my son?”

kings1.17.p7.b2.text: “O LORD my God, have You also brought tragedy on this widow who has opened her home to me, by causing her son to die?”

kings1.17.p7.b3.text: “O LORD my God, please let this boy’s life return to him!”

kings1.17.p7.b4.text: And the LORD listened to the voice of Elijah, and the child’s life returned to him, and he lived.

kings1.17.p8.b2.text: “Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is truth.”
